title: Palladis Chymicae Arcana Detecta: Marengus (PH165)
shelf_note: Italian-hand Latin alchemical manuscript of practical recipes (amalgams, mercury of metals, minerae); belongs on an alchemy shelf.
structure_note: Pages 107/207/308 carry manuscript folios 93/193/294: offset of 14 and 15 between pages 107, 207 and 308. That is consistent with front matter plus one extra leaf, not a splice. 16 of 418 pages untranslated.

title: Collection of Alchemical Texts: Flamel, Bernard, Llull (PH228)
shelf_note: 18th-century manuscript miscellany: Giorgi's Harmonia Mundi excerpted in French, Basil Valentine text, the Emerald Tablet. Alchemy/Hermetica.
structure_note: The OCR reads page numbers '1' (page 70) and '201' (page 212) for these pages. The miscellany seems to restart its pagination per tract, so printed numbers will not run straight. Page 212's photo is cropped at the right edge: line-ends are not visible.

title: Collection of Rosicrucian and Alchemical Texts (PH255)

structure_note: No printed page numbers in the OCR. 17 of 318 pages untranslated. The hand is heavily abbreviated with chemical symbols, and the OCR cannot read the symbols. That is a book-wide problem, not a structural one.

title: Paulum Athletam, ex I. Corinth. IX. comm. 26. 27. … MDCXXCIIX
shelf_note: Wittenberg-style philological dissertation (1688) on Paul as athlete, 1 Cor 9:26-27. No tradition or collection. Fits early-modern scholarship and classical philology, not the esoteric core.
structure_note: Printed pages 1215, 1218, 1223 run forward, consistent with a dissertation bound in a larger volume. 15 of 16 pages translated (presumably the title page is not). Nothing amiss.

tr_errors.english: They awarded ἆθλα for the nude games
tr_errors.problem: should be 'prizes for boxing'

tr_errors.english: Ignatius calls Hero an ἀθλητὴν <gloss>athlete</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: 'of God' lost: the point is the sacred use of the word

tr_errors.english: his more immediate origins
tr_errors.problem: 'its' (the word's) rendered 'his'

tr_errors.english: Men who are conquered are bound by the wrestling.
tr_errors.problem: ἀγρυξία is silence; it should read 'bound to silence', which is the point (nec audebant hiscere)

book_verdict: A good page set. The OCR handles dense Latin and Greek well, with a few Greek misreadings ('nude' for 'boxing', 'bound by wrestling' for 'bound to silence') that an expert would correct but that do not wreck the argument.
